children: Indian government bonds will likely extend losses on Thursday as oil above $100 a barrel has reignited supply and inflation concerns, even as a large liquidity surplus contains steeper losses.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to trade between 6.95% and 6.97%, a private-bank trader said, after ending at 6.9431% on Wednesday. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Brent crude futures hovered near a three-and-a-half-month high at $101.18 per barrel in Asian trade as an escalating Middle East conflict continued to ignite global fuel costs and energy supply disruptions.

Iran and the U.S. hit tankers in the biggest wave of attacks on shipping since the war began. Iran said on Wednesday it had attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. sank five Iranian oil tankers.

For India, the world's third-largest oil importer and consumer, higher crude prices threaten to swell the import bill, strain government finances, stoke inflation and sour sentiment across financial markets.
"The baseline scenario for oil is at $85 per barrel for us, so anything above that is an issue," said Kruti Chheta, Mumbai-based fund manager at Mirae Asset Mutual Fund.
Traders are now tracking the trajectory of energy prices, alongside U.S. and Indian inflation data and the Federal Reserve's policy decision due next week for further cues.
Bond markets see inflation risks skewed upward and are bracing for higher interest rates after the hawkish minutes of the Reserve Bank of India's August meeting.

The RBI must first reconcile its liquidity stance with its projected rate path, traders said, as ample liquidity, driven by overseas deposits raised by banks, has continued to push overnight rates lower.
To drain the system's cash surplus, currently at more than 10 trillion rupees, the RBI likely conducted near-maturity dollar-rupee sell-buy swaps on Wednesday, seven bankers said.
Overnight indexed swaps may also rise.
On Wednesday, the one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 5.9850%, the two-year (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) at 6.1850%, and the five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) at 6.48%.
